# Log Monitoring

A local React + FastAPI + SQLite prototype with two workflows: Upload & Analyze and Live Monitoring.

## Processing and infrastructure disclosure

**This implementation is fully simulated.** Seeded logs, cloud metadata, classifications, scores, and local investigation responses are generated by this application. No AWS resources are created, no SSH connections are attempted, and no trained model or repository weights are loaded. The EC2-style instance IDs, private addresses, regions, and hostnames describe simulated sources; they are not reachable cloud instances. The interface uses normal product language as requested, without demo/mock badges.

Reference collections contain 12,000 generated messages each for BGL, HDFS, Liberty, and Thunderbird (48,000 total). These are dataset-shaped examples, not copies of the original research datasets. Three independent sources start with 10,000 historical messages each and continue producing records while running. Add Server creates another local simulated source with its own cursor and history. Profiles describe log formats and sequence grouping, not AWS instance types or machine capabilities.

Classification uses deterministic failure-pattern scenarios, not a trained detector. The scores are fixed illustrative values and are not calibrated probabilities. Profile metrics are computed from generated evaluation records; they are not published research metrics or evidence of model accuracy. Uploaded ground truth is used only for evaluation. Explicit imported predictions attached to a sequence override the simulation for that sequence; imported scores are retained only with those predictions.

## Run

From this directory:

```sh
uv venv .venv
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements.txt
npm --prefix frontend install
npm --prefix frontend run build
./run.sh
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The initial database seed happens once. SQLite lives in `runtime/observatory.sqlite3`; set `OBSERVATORY_DB` to choose another location. Stop the server before copying the database, or use SQLite's backup API. Do not delete the database to restart streaming: source cursors and partial sequences resume automatically without duplicating events. Start/stop state is retained across restarts; downtime is not backfilled. Use one application worker so there is only one scheduler.

Development: `npm --prefix frontend run dev` proxies API calls to port 8000. Production frontend changes require a rebuild. Tests: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q`.

## Upload & Analyze

Choose BGL, HDFS, Liberty, or Thunderbird. Upload a raw `.log`/`.txt` file or prepared CSV/JSON sequences (20 MB browser limit). Raw messages are validated against the selected profile's timestamp/structure. HDFS raw messages require block IDs and are grouped across the file by `blk_...`; a message mentioning multiple blocks belongs to each relevant block session. Other raw profiles use consecutive 100-message windows and retain a final partial window. Prepared sequences preserve supplied boundaries.

CSV/JSON column mapping supports sequence ID, content/logs, prediction, score, ground truth, original timestamp, and block ID. JSON content can be an array of message strings. CSV content can contain messages separated by ` ;-; ` or newlines. Keep predictions and ground truth in distinct columns. Example JSON:

```json
[
  {"sequence_id":"request-1","logs":["INFO request completed"],"ground_truth":"normal"},
  {"sequence_id":"request-2","logs":["ERROR connection refused"],"prediction":"anomalous","score":0.91,"ground_truth":"anomalous"}
]
```

A background job moves queued → processing → completed, committing results in batches of eight sequences. Progress reflects records actually processed. Results support search, pagination, evidence, investigation chat, and full-run CSV/JSON exports. Original raw messages remain unchanged. Ground truth is never used to generate classifications. Exports include processing origin and separate prediction/ground-truth fields.

## Live Monitoring and investigation

Servers have independent start/stop and 1/10/50 messages-per-second controls. Pause display stops browser updates while collection continues. The feed supports server, time, severity, classification, and text filters. Incoming severity is an event field; anomaly classification belongs to a completed sequence. The browser retains at most 200 live records, and older records are available through cursor pagination. The anomaly inbox and View Logs/Ask AI actions always identify the specific completed sequence.

Local chat uses deterministic scenario responses based on the actual sequence evidence, with numbered references, estimated severity, possible causes, checks, and prevention. It is not a general-purpose language model and cannot establish a root cause. Unsupported questions acknowledge insufficient evidence. Conversations persist per result.

The existing optional hosted integration uses the OpenAI Responses API. Only setting **both** `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` enables external calls. Evidence and conversation context then leave the local machine when Ask AI is used. For entirely local operation, leave the key empty. To enable hosted chat, edit `web/.env` with your key and model, then restart using `./run.sh`; the launcher loads that private file. Direct uvicorn commands require these variables to be exported separately. The `.env` file is ignored by Git; `.env.example` contains only empty-key setup guidance. Credentials remain on the backend. Provider failures produce an error without saving a false reply. See [Responses API documentation](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses).

## Storage, APIs, and migration

New data uses `v2_*` tables, separating profiles (code configuration), collections, sequences, server identities, runs, results, events, and conversations. Processing origins are `generated_scenario`, `profile_simulation`, `imported_prediction`, or `mixed` at collection level. Chat origins are `scenario_response` and `hosted_ai`. A future inference adapter can produce the same result fields with a distinct origin without changing UI contracts.

Previous prototype tables are retained unchanged apart from pausing previously running sources/sessions. History → Open archive exposes their preserved results. Old records are never renamed or promoted to new classifications. The legacy backend and replay script are not included in this package.

- `GET /api/overview`: compact counts, profile metrics, server health, activity.
- `GET /api/stream`: SSE revision notifications; no full log history payload.
- `GET /api/logs`: indexed server/time/severity filters and before/after ID cursors, capped at 200 rows.
- `GET /api/results`: server/run/classification/text filtering and pagination.
- `POST /api/collections`, `POST /api/collections/{id}/analyze`: import and queued processing.
- `GET /api/runs`, `/api/runs/{id}`, `/api/runs/{id}/export`: history, progress, exports.
- `POST /api/servers`, `/api/servers/{id}/control`: source creation and controls.
- `GET /api/results/{id}`, `POST /api/results/{id}/chat`: evidence and persistent conversation.

SQLite transactions persist event insertion and source position together, with uniqueness constraints on run/sequence/line to prevent duplicates. Background processing and indexed queries keep history off the rendering path. Classification-filtered live views refresh a bounded page so newly completed older events are not missed; unfiltered live views use incremental ID batches. Text substring search scans matching records; this local prototype is not designed for unlimited production retention. It has no multi-user authentication and binds to loopback by default.

## Upload-only four-detector comparison

New upload and reference analyses offer **Analyze with all four models**, enabled by default. Completed upload runs can be compared later using **Compare models** in their results view. Live runs cannot create comparison jobs and their detector remains unchanged.

The comparison explicitly displays **Simulated**. BERT + Llama, DeepLog, LogBERT, and the rule-based baseline are names for illustrative adapters, not loaded implementations or real benchmark results. Version `simulation-v1` uses four deterministic policies: failure phrases/service-impact language; repeated failure messages or failures after recovery; critical language or diverse failure events; and the existing baseline patterns. Repetition normalizes numbers. These policies intentionally produce disagreements without using labels, imported predictions, random scores, or target metrics.

Each upload sequence, including normal ones, gets four independent records with its unchanged sequence ID/boundaries. `comparison_jobs` persists the run and processing cursor; `comparison_predictions` stores detector ID/version, origin, status, prediction, policy reason, and failures. Primary predictions and imported records remain untouched. The adapter input is profile plus message strings only; future real adapters must use distinct origins and versions, and must not share a simulated evaluation cohort.

Metrics use anomalous as the positive class and the intersection of labeled sequences successfully completed by all four adapters of the same simulation version/origin. Coverage reports total, completed by all four, evaluated, unlabeled, and labeled pending/failed counts. The UI shows N/A for undefined denominators and requests ground truth when no labels exist. No failed or pending result is counted as normal. During processing, metrics describe the explicitly shown completed cohort. The interface shows per-detector precision, recall, F1, and accuracy cards plus a grouped percentage bar chart with metric selection. Missing metrics appear as N/A, never as zero; confusion counts remain available in exports.

API additions:

- `POST /api/collections/{id}/analyze` accepts optional `{ "compare": true }` (default true).
- `POST /api/runs/{id}/comparison` creates or returns the upload run's comparison job idempotently.
- `GET /api/runs/{id}/comparison` returns progress, coverage, per-detector status and metrics, or null when no job exists.
- `GET /api/runs/{id}/comparison/results` supports `search`, `filter=all|disagreement|flagged`, `page`, and `size` (maximum 100).
- `GET /api/runs/{id}/comparison/export?format=json|csv` exports predictions and shared-cohort metrics. CSV uses explicit metrics/prediction record types.
- Sequence evidence includes `comparisons`; chat context includes policy reasons, versions, and simulation origins. Existing conversations are preserved; subsequent questions receive current comparison context.

Comparison computation itself makes no model/network calls. Explicit Ask AI interactions continue to use the configured local or hosted chat provider. Tests in `tests/test_comparison.py` cover all four reference collections (48,000 messages), labels, failures, restart recovery, determinism, metrics, exports, and live-run isolation.

### Recommended actions in analysis results

Upload results and four-detector comparison tables include a **Recommended action** column. Suggestions are generated locally from parsed message content, with expandable checklists and numbered evidence. Categories cover listener/port conflicts, DNS, connection failures, TLS, permissions, explicit configuration errors, storage integrity, and resource limits. Up to three supported categories are shown per sequence. The original result table follows its original classification; the comparison table recommends investigation when any completed detector flags the sequence. Pending/failed comparisons without a flag are identified as incomplete.

These are investigation suggestions, not a network audit or confirmed root cause. No service settings, ports, firewall rules, or credentials are inspected or modified. Normal results suggest monitoring, and unknown anomalies request more evidence instead of inventing a configuration fault. The `recommended_action` object contains title, summary, basis, origin (`evidence_rules`), and issues with checks/evidence. Live result tables remain unchanged.

## Integration status

Live streams are simulated. Real EC2 ingestion and trained-model inference are not yet connected. The optional hosted investigation chat is separate from anomaly classification. Large generated sample logs are excluded; the BGL label test generates its own temporary fixture.
